extracted.intended_audience: Parliamentarians, policymakers, writers, publishers, and the literate public in 17th‑century England (and those interested in printing/licensing policy)
extracted.subtask_description: Argumentative guidance against licensing and censorship of printed works, advocating open publication, public disputation, toleration of non‑fundamental differences, and the institutional limits of controllers of the press.

rubrics_metrics.name: Freedom_of_writing_and_exercise
rubrics_metrics.description: Our faith and knowledge thrives by exercise; 'Truth is compar'd in Scripture to a dreaming fountain; if her waters flow not in a perpetuall progression, they sicken into a muddy pool of conformity and tradition.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permit ongoing writing, disputation, and publication as necessary practices to keep knowledge vital and moving; restriction will stagnate truth and learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid_suppression_which_enhances_authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The punishing of wits enhances their authority ... a forbidden writing is thought to be a certain spark of truth that flies up in the faces of them who seeke to tread it out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not suppress or punish writings simply to silence them; prohibition can amplify the influence and perceived legitimacy of those writings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licensing_deterrence_to_learned_men
rubrics_metrics.description: Liberty of writing should be restrain'd by a discipline ... will after a while be afraid of every conventicle ... give cause of doubt and discouragement to all learned and religious men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that licensing chills scholarly and religious authorship and will discourage serious contributors from publishing their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open_publication_maintains_known_truths
rubrics_metrics.description: This order ... by disinabling us to the maintenance of what is known already.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow open publication so that established truths can be exercised, defended, and kept alive through continual engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing_more_public_and_refutable_than_preaching
rubrics_metrics.description: Writing is more publick then preaching; and more easie to refutation, if need be, there being so many whose businesse and profession meerly it is, to be the champions of Truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor written publication as a forum where arguments are visible, can be examined, and refuted publicly, improving epistemic accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open_debate_keeps_clergy_vigilant
rubrics_metrics.description: If a bold book may now and then issue forth ... it will concern [a minister] then to keep waking ... fearing lest any of his flock be seduc't, who also then would be better instructed, better exercis'd and disciplin'd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow alternative writings because they spur established teachers to diligence and prevent intellectual complacency among religious instructors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid_concentrated_licensing_power
rubrics_metrics.description: Should ye set an Oligarchy of twenty ingrossers over it, to bring a famin upon our minds again ... they who counsell ye to such a suppressing, doe as good as bid ye suppress yourselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not vest control of publishing in a small body (oligarchy/licencer board) because it risks intellectual starvation and self‑suppression by the polity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tolerate_nonfundamental_differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Those neighboring differences, or rather indifferences, are what I speak of, whether in some point of doctrine or of discipline, which though they may be many, yet need not interrupt the unity of Spirit ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish between matters that are impious/evil (which may be prohibited) and neighboring doctrinal or disciplinary differences (which should be tolerated to preserve unity and charity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Test_truth_in_open_encounter
rubrics_metrics.description: Let her and Falshood grapple ... Who ever knew Truth put to the worst, in a free and open encounter?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow truth and error to face each other publicly; confidence in truth's strength is a reason to permit free disputation rather than resort to prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suppression_as_cowardice_in_pursuit_of_truth
rubrics_metrics.description: To keep a narrow bridge of licencing ... is but weakness and cowardice in the wars of Truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid procedural barriers that enable opponents to evade public argument; require open argument rather than administrative gatekeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid_rigid_external_conformity
rubrics_metrics.description: While we still affect by all means a rigid externall formality, we may as soon fall again into a gross conforming stupidity, a stark and dead congealment ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from enforcing outward uniformity by law; such enforced conformity can produce intellectual deadness worse than many sectarian divisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do_not_limit_where_truth_may_appear
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither is God appointed and confin'd, where and out of what place these his chosen shall be first heard to speak; for he sees not as man sees, chooses not as man chooses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not restrict the venues or persons from which revelation or important argument may arise; institutional monopolies on authority risk missing truth from unexpected sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be_open_to_new_voices_during_reformation
rubrics_metrics.description: When God shakes a Kingdome ... God then raises to his own work men of rare abilities ... not only to look back and revise what hath been taught heretofore, but to gain further and goe on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During periods of reform or upheaval, permit a wider range of voices because important, novel insights often come from new or unexpected authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Printing_prohibition_hinders_importation_of_truth
rubrics_metrics.description: It hinders and retards the importation of our richell Marchandize, Truth; nay it was first established ... little differing from that policie wherewith the Turk upholds his Alcoran by the prohibition of Printing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that prohibiting printing blocks the flow of useful knowledge and resembles the censorship practices of regimes that intend to keep populations uninformed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Moderate_toleration_promotes_unity_and_learning
rubrics_metrics.description: A little generous prudence, a little forbearance of one another, and some grain of charity might win all these diligences to joyn, and unite in one generall and brotherly learn h after Truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate prudence, forbearance, and charity to help divergent thinkers collaborate and contribute constructively to the common pursuit of truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plurality_as_sign_of_learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is much desire to learn, there of necessity will be much arguing, much writing, many opinions; for opinion in good men is but knowledge in the making.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the proliferation of opinions in a learned community as a positive sign of intellectual vitality and progress, not as grounds for suppression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discourage_outsourcing_of_conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: A wealthy man ... to find himself out from factor, to whose care and credit he may commit the whole managing of his religious affairs ... makes the very person of that man his religion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warn against structures (including licensing regimes) that encourage individuals to transfer responsibility for conscience and belief to authorities or gatekeepers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licencing_likely_to_forbid_truth_itself
rubrics_metrics.description: If it come to prohibiting, there is not ought more likely to be prohibited then truth itself; whose first appearance to our eyes, blear'd and dimmed with prejudice and custom, is more unsightly and unplausible than many errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be cautious: institutional prohibition tends to target novel or unpopular truths precisely because they appear unfamiliar or unattractive at first; this counsels restraint in enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Licencing_imposes_unmanageable_burden
rubrics_metrics.description: How much it hurts and hinders the licencers themselves in the calling of their Ministry ... of necessity they must neglect either the one duty or the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge practical limits: assigning licensing duties (often to clergy or officials) will conflict with their other obligations and create administrative dysfunction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer_public_reasoning_over_statutory_hearing_only
rubrics_metrics.description: Ye cannot make us now lesse capable ... unleese ye first make your selves ... oppressive, arbitrary, and tyrannous, as they were from whom ye have freed us. Give me the liberty to know, to utter, and to argue freely according to conscience, above all liberties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect the civic liberty to read, speak, and argue freely; safeguard public reasoning as a higher priority than statutory or administrative gatekeeping of speech.
